coverage:
Read in full: Sec 1 (inputs), Sec 2 (full-box susceptibility), Sec 4 (renewal), Sec 6 (fast bridges), Sec 9 (completion), plus the key parts of Sec 5 (S_2 corollaries) and Sec 7 (small returns, many-bridges lemma, local mass, temporal modulus). Checked in detail:
- Sec 9: the exact-length transfer Z_n >= 1 (submultiplicativity plus the contradiction with B_h ~ h^{-1/4}), and every deduction in the section: diameter, local-mass lower/upper bounds, covering lower/upper bounds, dimension corollary, R_g identity and lower bound, moments.
- Sec 4 renewal: irreducible tail bound, overshoot (l/x)^{3/4}, second moment E N_h^2 <= C h^{3/2}, K-trial exponent -17θ/64 (computed), conditioning bound C_R(n) <= C R^{1/2} giving (R/H)^{1/2}, the explicit choice θ=ε/8, ξ=ε/4, and the upper bound via the h^{13/12}/B_H first moment.
- Sec 2 full box: ρφ ≈ 0.876 < 1; the Fibonacci no-west count; the cone and integer-row displacement; eligibility of the one-arc parameters; the HW strip bound exp(CW^{3/4}); convergence of the run/strip series.
- Sec 6 fast chain: exponent H^{3/4}Π(s/H)^{1/4}, the good/bad turn factor table, the both-bad identity, the untreated-retreat bound -13/80, and the gain-charging argument.
- Sec 5: S_2 exponent 3/4, consistent with the SLE boundary arm exponents x_2 - 2x_1 = 2 - 5/4.
- Sec 7: the many-bridges reflection construction (period (0,2md_0), essential separating polygons); the local-mass bound a^2/log H against a log H (log j ~ log H because j >= a/D); the 4/3 conversion in the modulus.
Not verified line by line: the Sec 5 induction and the Sec 3 sewing/corridor constructions. Companion inputs were taken as given.
main_claim: With uniform probability on n-step self-avoiding walks on the honeycomb lattice, for every δ, k > 0 there is an event of probability at least 1 - C n^{-k} on which: the diameter is n^{3/4±δ}; the local mass M(z,s) is within n^{±δ} of min{n, s^{4/3}}; and the covering number N(s) is within n^{±δ} of 1 + n s^{-4/3}, uniformly over visited z and s in [1,n]. Corollaries cover directional spans, covering dimension 4/3, and the radius of gyration and moments.
